kurz: Lentils need no soaking and cook in 10 to 30 minutes: red ones collapse into a purée, dark ones hold their shape.
bild_im_kopf: Like buttons with and without a coat: without their skin the red ones dissolve, the dark ones keep their shell.
was_passiert: Lentils are small and flat, so water quickly reaches the centre. Red and yellow lentils are hulled and split: their starch [[quellen|swells]] freely and they fall apart. Beluga, green and brown lentils have a firm skin and stay whole.
warum_wichtig: Choosing the variety to suit the dish gets you soup or salad and not accidentally the opposite.
faustregeln: For salads: use beluga or green lentils and cook them just tender.
For dal and soup: red lentils, they turn creamy by themselves.
If lentils stay hard, acid or very hard water is often to blame.
schritte: Rinse the lentils in a sieve and pick out any small stones.
Put them in plenty of water or stock and simmer gently.
Red lentils about 10 to 15 minutes, dark ones 20 to 30 minutes (as a guide).
Salt can go in early; add acid such as vinegar or tomatoes only at the end.
